entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Apollodorus of Artemita was a Greek historian who flourished between 130 and 87 BC. Hailing from the Greco-Parthian city of Artemita in Apolloniatis and a citizen of the Parthian Empire, he is best known for his work on the 'Bibliotheca' and its contribution to the compilation of Greek and Roman mythology.

Born in the late 2nd century BC, Apollodorus' life was marked by his interactions with prominent figures of the time, including the Roman Emperor Augustus.

Through his writings, Apollodorus sought to legitimize the Parthian Empire and its cultural heritage, reflecting the complex dynamics of the ancient world.

Apollodorus' legacy extends beyond his own works, influencing later historians and scholars in their understanding of ancient Greek and Roman mythology.

The historian's own life was cut short when he died at the age of 99, leaving behind a vast body of work that continues to captivate scholars and enthusiasts alike.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Apollodorus of Artemita's work on the 'Bibliotheca' helped to consolidate Greek and Roman mythology, contributing to the development of a shared cultural heritage between the two civilizations. His legacy extends beyond his own works, influencing later historians and scholars in their understanding of ancient Greek and Roman mythology.
